c2.evidence: Concrete: 9% on item+shipping, $0.10 min, $150 max, free to list

maximize: List with precise catalog data — pressing, label, catalog number, matrix runout — because Discogs buyers search by exact release and premium pressings sell for multiples. The $150 fee cap makes Discogs cheap for high-value records: a $2,000 grail costs $150 here vs. $180+ at 9% elsewhere. Keep shipping charges honest and minimal (use media mail in the US) since the fee applies to shipping too. Grade conservatively per the Goldmine standard — overgraded records get returned and cost you double shipping. Build seller feedback with cheap records first; high feedback unlocks trust for big-ticket sales.

List for sale with Goldmine-graded condition and fair shipping

timing: Paid at sale; fees deducted automatically
who_pays: The buyer pays through PayPal, and Discogs deducts its fee automatically before the money reaches you.
who_qualifies: Anyone 18+ with music to sell (vinyl, CDs, cassettes).
work_available: Discogs' marketplace is active and open to new sellers — the Discogs database drives buyer intent.
what_gets_accepted: Listings are accepted for legal music items with exact catalog data (pressing, label, matrix) to appear in searches. Circumventing the marketplace via private messages means account suspension.
costs_and_unpaid_time: Official: 9% fee on both item price and shipping, minimum $0.10, maximum $150 per order — records over ~$1,667 effectively get a lower rate. PayPal's own processing sits on top of the Discogs fee. Unpaid time goes to cataloging, grading, listing, packing, and shipping.
when_cash_arrives: At sale — fees are deducted automatically from the buyer's PayPal payment, and the net reaches you right away.
